sn20.7:1.2: The Dasārahas were probably the people known in Sanskrit as the Daśārṇa of the western Vindhya mountains. | The _mudiṅga_ is a double-headed drum known today as _mridangam_, which is still widely used in southern India. It is named for the paste (“mud”, today called the _karanai_) applied to one of the heads that gives it its distinctive snare-like tone (_chapu_). The skin is attached with a wooden rim tightened with leather straps. | _Āṇaka_ is another name for what is said to be a large military drum, which might be named after _āṇi_ in the sense of “tuning peg”, a feature of the modern _mardala_. However, in this case, the context requires that the _āṇi_ be a plug for patching the shell, after which the drum was named “Plugger”.
sn20.7:1.4: The _pokkhara_ is the “drumskin”. The _phalaka_ is the “wooden shell”, a single hollowed-out log from which the _mridangam_ is constructed.
